abstract.t: This document defines a vendor-neutral data model and a state machine for orchestrating coordinated post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithm and key rotation across multiple IETF protocol surfaces within a single administrative domain. Protocol surfaces in scope include TLS 1.3, IKEv2, COSE, JOSE, and X.509 PKI. The model introduces the notion of a rotation epoch, a cross-protocol dependency graph, and a rollback gate.

The mechanism is intended to be implementable by orchestration controllers and is intentionally interface-only. Concrete trigger weights, carve-out parameters, and tenant policy values remain operator-specific and are not disclosed in this Internet-Draft.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Enterprise migrations to post-quantum cryptography require coordinated rotation across many protocol surfaces. Today, each surface defines rotation independently, leading to inconsistent posture across an administrative domain. This document defines an orchestration layer above existing surface-specific rotation mechanisms.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD", "MAY" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

section.name: Rotation Epoch Data Model
section.t: A rotation epoch is identified by an opaque rotation_epoch_id string and bound to a set of (protocol, algorithm, parameter) tuples. The data model is expressed in YANG with a JSON instance encoding for controller-to-controller exchange.

section.name: Cross-Protocol Dependency Graph
section.t: Surfaces MAY declare dependencies on other surfaces such that a rotation event on a parent surface gates rotation of children. The graph is acyclic. Cycles MUST be rejected by the orchestration controller.

section.name: Rollback Gate
section.t: Each rotation transition includes a rollback gate that specifies the maximum time and error rate beyond which a rotation MUST be reversed. Concrete numeric values for rollback thresholds are deployment-specific and are not disclosed in this Internet-Draft.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Orchestration controllers become high-value targets and MUST be hardened accordingly. The interface specified here does not transport private-key material; controllers SHOULD use mutual TLS and short-lived credentials.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests IANA to establish a Post-Quantum Rotation Orchestration Registry under the Security area, containing surface identifiers, dependency relation codes, and standard rollback-gate parameter names.
